items.q: Which statement about investigations in ADPKD is correct?
opts: RFT is normal, USG is the investigation of choice, and MRI evaluates the risk for ESRD
RFT is always raised with USG being only supportive
MRI is the investigation of choice for diagnosis, USG for risk
CT scan is the investigation of choice for diagnosis
items.exp: ADPKD investigations: RFT normal; USG the IOC; MRI to evaluate the risk for ESRD; CT scan and CT urography for renal stones; FDG PET to find the source of infection in cyst infection. (Book p788)

items.q: A 34-year-old with a family history of ADPKD has no cysts on ultrasound. Which investigation confirms that he can safely donate a kidney?
opts: MRI — more than 30 years old with not even one cyst on MRI means he can donate a kidney
Repeat ultrasound after 6 months to look for newly appearing renal cysts
CT urography showing both kidneys and the collecting systems clearly
Genetic testing of the PKD3 locus to exclude an inherited ADPKD mutation
items.exp: Criteria to rule out ADPKD if family history is present but USG shows no cysts: >30 years with not even one cyst on MRI — such a person can donate a kidney. (Book p788)

items.q: Match each ADPKD investigation with its purpose — 1) MRI  2) CT scan and CT urography  3) FDG PET scan … A) To evaluate risk for ESRD  B) Renal stones  C) To find the source of infection (cyst infection)
items.exp: MRI evaluates risk for ESRD; CT scan and CT urography evaluate renal stones; FDG PET scan finds the source of infection in cyst infection. (Book p788)

items.q: A patient with ADPKD and fever with loin pain is suspected to have cyst infection; blood cultures are negative. Which investigation is used to localise the source of infection?
items.exp: FDG PET scan is used 'to find source of infection'—cyst infection in ADPKD. (Book p788)

items.q: The rationale behind reducing osmolality in the treatment of ADPKD is:
opts: To reduce ADH, since cystic growth depends on ADH
To reduce blood pressure by natriuresis
To prevent hyperkalaemia from renin excess
To reduce the risk of hepatic cysts
items.exp: Treatment of ADPKD begins with ↓osmolality to reduce ADH, because cystic growth depends on ADH. (Book p788)

items.q: The daily fluid intake advised to lower osmolality in ADPKD is:
items.exp: ↓Osmolality in ADPKD: ↑fluid intake 4–5 L/day, along with tolvaptan (DOC). (Book p788)

items.q: The drug of choice in the treatment of ADPKD, and its class, are:
opts: Tolvaptan — an oral V₂ antagonist, 15 mg at night, monitoring LFT
Vaptan — an oral V₁ agonist, 30 mg in the morning
Everolimus — used as the drug of choice
items.exp: Tolvaptan is the DOC in ADPKD: oral V₂ antagonist, 15 mg at night with LFT monitoring. Somatostatin analogues and everolimus are novel therapies. (Book p788)

items.q: A patient with ADPKD is started on the drug of choice for cyst growth. Which baseline and follow-up monitoring is required?
opts: Liver function tests, since tolvaptan is an oral V₂ antagonist given at 15 mg at night
Serum amylase, since tolvaptan causes pancreatitis
ECG for QT prolongation, with 40 mg twice daily dosing
items.exp: Tolvaptan (oral V₂ antagonist, 15 mg at night) requires monitoring of LFT. (Book p788)

items.q: Match each ADPKD therapy with its role — 1) Tolvaptan  2) Everolimus and somatostatin analogues  3) ACE inhibitor or ARB … A) Tight BP control  B) Oral V2 antagonist, 15 mg at night with LFT monitoring  C) Novel therapies
items.exp: Treatment: tolvaptan (oral V2 antagonist, 15 mg at night, monitor LFT) is the DOC for cyst growth; somatostatin analogues and everolimus are novel therapies; tight BP control (SBP 95-110/DBP 60-75 mmHg) uses an ACE inhibitor or ARB. (Book p788)

items.q: In the ADPKD treatment section, tight BP control means a target of:
items.exp: Tight BP control in ADPKD: SBP 95–110/DBP 60–75 mmHg using an ACE inhibitor or ARB. (Book p788)

items.q: The antihypertensive classes specified for tight BP control in ADPKD are:
opts: Calcium channel blocker or beta blocker
Alpha blocker or centrally acting agent
items.exp: Tight BP control (SBP 95–110/DBP 60–75 mmHg) in ADPKD is achieved with an ACE inhibitor or ARB. (Book p788)

items.q: All but one of the following are part of the treatment or prevention plan in ADPKD. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: Treatment of ADPKD: ↓osmolality with fluids and tolvaptan, tight BP control with ACEi/ARB, novel therapies (somatostatin analogues, everolimus) and potassium citrate; steroids have no role. (Book p788)

items.q: Which three measures are listed under prevention of complications in ADPKD?
opts: Watch for abdominal pain, avoid blunt trauma to prevent rupture, and potassium citrate to alkalinise urine and prevent stones
Avoid fluids, use NSAIDs for pain control, and start dialysis early in every patient
Prophylactic nephrectomy, lifelong prophylactic antibiotics, and strict bed rest at home
Vaccination against streptococci, statins for cholesterol control, and daily aspirin
items.exp: Prevention of complications in ADPKD: watch out for abdominal pain; avoid blunt trauma (to prevent rupture); potassium citrate for alkalinisation of urine (to prevent renal stones). (Book p788)

items.q: Fill up: In ADPKD, potassium citrate is given to ______ the urine and prevent renal stones.
items.exp: Prevention of complications in ADPKD: potassium citrate causes alkalinisation of the urine to prevent renal stones. (Book p788)

items.q: An ADPKD patient who plays contact sports asks about precautions. The correct advice from the prevention list is:
opts: Avoid blunt trauma to the abdomen to prevent cyst rupture, and report abdominal pain early
Continue all activities because rupture never occurs
Take NSAIDs before activity to prevent pain
items.exp: Prevention list: watch out for abdominal pain and avoid blunt trauma (to prevent rupture of cysts). (Book p788)
